guide: Open Start and type your business name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the weekly hours cap, the minimum booking, the rest days between births and the share over plan that you accept.
Check Packages, Areas and Doulas. They hold the planned hours of each package, the mileage rate of each area and the weekly cap of each doula that the other sheets read.
Write every visit in Visits: date, start time, client, doula, kind, hours, miles and area. The week, the mileage cost and the short and complete checks fill in by themselves.
Write each birth in Births Attended: the call, arrival and leave times, the hours and the miles. The minutes to arrive, the night call and the quarter fill in. Nothing else about a birth is recorded.
Keep Hour Packs up to date with the hours used and any extra hours. Hour Pack Ledger shows the hours left, the expiry check and the amount ready to invoice.
Open Hours by Phase to see every client against the package plan, and Weekly Hours by Doula to see who is over the weekly cap.
Read Mileage by Month, Mileage by Client and Mileage by Doula and Area when you set a travel fee or check the mileage you pay.
Use Births per Month, Rest Days Between Births, Birth Hours Bands and Call Time Bands to see how many births you attend, how much rest follows and when calls come.
Use the 18 tools to compare hours with the plan, plan next week, test a travel fee, check rest, plan pack expiry and forecast the next 4 weeks.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Hours Dashboard and the charts every week. A solo doula uses the same sheets with one doula and no backup rota.

listing.title: Doula Business Visits, Hours, Mileage and Births Excel Template: Hour Pack Ledger, Weekly Hours Cap, Mileage Log, Birth Log
listing.headline: Know the real hours behind every package, visit and birth
listing.description:
Keep track of the hours your doula business really takes in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-doula who also takes clients, contracted doulas, backup doulas and a part-time admin, and just as useful for a solo doula who wants a personal time and mileage log. Visits records every prenatal, postpartum, night and debrief visit with hours, miles and area. Births Attended records the call, arrival and leave times, the hours and the miles of each birth, with no detail beyond that. Hour Packs and the Hour Pack Ledger show hours bought, used and left for every prepaid pack (a set number of postpartum hours bought together), the expiry check and the extra hours as an invoice-ready amount.

Hours by Phase sets every client against the planned hours of the package. Weekly Hours by Doula counts visit and birth hours against the weekly cap and the weeks over it in a row. Mileage by Month, by Client and by Doula and Area show the mileage cost and its share of the package price. Rest Days Between Births, Births per Month, Birth Hours Bands and Call Time Bands show how many births are attended, how much rest follows and when the calls come.

18 tools answer the weekly questions: actual hours against plan, the postpartum hours ledger, the weekly hours load, mileage totals and a travel fee test, the births attended summary, rest days, visit hours by kind, pack expiry and pace, extra hours to invoice, visit length, area clustering, birth hours, call-to-arrival time, night work, prenatal visit timing, a 4-week hours forecast and yearly hours per doula. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to clients, doulas, backup doulas, the admin, the owner-doula and the accountant.

This is part five of the Doula Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Clients appear by name, area and dates only, with no medical detail. It helps you keep track of hours, dates, money and capacity and does not promise any result. Check your local rules for records, insurance and tax.

charge every month and hide the hours, mileage and rest-day logic behind reports you cannot change
